messages.author: 6eb170ca555d9bdd
messages.subject: Random Forest Variable Importance
parts:
Hi Davis R Users,

I suspect that the following question is unanswerable without actually modifying the source code of randomForest to save individual variable importance measures per CART model, but maybe I’m wrong.

Basically, I’m looking for a way to obtain individual variable importance on a tree-by-tree basis rather than the summarized output of importance(my_rf_model). I would like this so I can make cumulative variable importance animations directly from randomForestobjects (see animation below with mtcars).  

If you think this is a good question, please consider upvoting it on stack overflow to give it more attention, and if you know an answer, that’s even better!

Regards,
Rich

messages.author: 5f533b50135a7f86
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Random Forest Variable Importance
parts:
Hi Rich et al., 

I spent half an hour looking into this last night, after your posted the question on Twitter.  It looks even worse than modifying the source code:  variable importance seems to be calculated in the underlying C code, in the loop that constructs each tree in the forest.  The C didn’t look too bad, but was still more trouble than I have time for now.  :-/

Hopefully someone on here comes up with a better approach!  

Dan

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Random Forest Variable Importance
parts:
Hi Rich, don't you need the entire collection of trees to calculate a legitimate variable importance measure from random forest?  

Because, as the method goes, each individual tree is randomly leaving out predictors, sometimes very "important" ones, along the way...

Scott

That's correct Scott.

I want the individual importances so I can calculate a cumulative importance to show (visually) how the importances accumulate over time and converge on a final list of ranked variables. In practice, I don't use the individual scores for anything other than communicating how a RF calculates this summarized score as the aggregation of importance scores over many trees.

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Random Forest Variable Importance
parts:
Hi Rich, I agree that what you want does not appear to be saved in the object returned by a call to randomForest.  

Since this is just for didactic purposes, you could use counts of the variables used to split nodes in each tree to scale the final importance scores across all trees.  You can get the splitting variables from the getTree function.

Scott
